story.title: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk

facts.text: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has data centers full of memory, but seemingly it's the 32GB of RAM in your desktop that's the problem.
In an interview over beers with the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, Altman said that local inference, and, by extension, people having DRAM in computers at home, is "quite terrible."

OpenAI isn't exactly threatened by some laptops and gaming rigs just yet, but local AI could mean people one day paying less for subscriptions to models like GPT-6 Luna if they have the power to run them at home.

Altman's talk suggests that the company would prefer that more RAM go to OpenAI's data centers rather than home computers, which also sparks enthusiast fears of not being able to own your own hardware or software, but rather rent an agent and a computer in the cloud.
Some of what Altman is saying is based on an idea that data center buildouts won't slow down.
It also assumes that RAM being used in AI data centers 24/7 is more worthwhile than RAM that is used for spreadsheets, web browsing, gaming, and maybe even local AI occasionally.
The rest of the wide-ranging interview includes talk of this week's PHP vulnerabilities, sandboxing models in training, and OpenAI's research in mathematics.
Freedman is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware focusing on laptops, desktops and gaming.
A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others.

Asked about supply chain shortages, like the ongoing RAM shortage, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview that it’s “terrible” to have RAM in personal PCs instead of data centers.

Right now, memory companies Samsung and SK Hynix have long term deals with cloud service operators and projects like OpenAI’s Stargate that have reserved much of the world’s RAM output over the next few years.
From a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time.
You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment, - Sam Altman .
Remarks come as AI infrastructure providers compete for increasingly limited memory supplies.
Memory manufacturers are prioritizing demand from data centers, putting additional pressure on the consumer market and contributing to higher prices for PCs and other hardware.
In other words, Altman believes memory would be put to better use in centralized data centers, where it could continuously serve multiple users and workloads.
However, his argument focuses on local AI inference and does not account for the many other reasons people need RAM in their PCs, including gaming, everyday applications and multitasking.
Altman’s claim that idle consumer RAM wastes a global resource draws scrutiny given OpenAI’s direct financial stake in cloud computing
Altman reportedly argued on the Cheeky Pint podcast that local AI inference creates a poor allocation of scarce DRAM .

sources.title: OpenAI CEO says it's 'quite terrible' for your PC to have RAM — Sam Altman says data centers offer better utilization - Tom's Hardware
passages: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has data centers full of memory, but seemingly it's the 32GB of RAM in your desktop that's the problem.
In an interview over beers with the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, Altman said that local inference, and, by extension, people having DRAM in computers at home, is "quite terrible."

OpenAI isn't exactly threatened by some laptops and gaming rigs just yet, but local AI could mean people one day paying less for subscriptions to models like GPT-6 Luna if they have the power to run them at home.

Altman's talk suggests that the company would prefer that more RAM go to OpenAI's data centers rather than home computers, which also sparks enthusiast fears of not being able to own your own hardware or software, but rather rent an agent and a computer in the cloud.
Some of what Altman is saying is based on an idea that data center buildouts won't slow down.
It also assumes that RAM being used in AI data centers 24/7 is more worthwhile than RAM that is used for spreadsheets, web browsing, gaming, and maybe even local AI occasionally.
The rest of the wide-ranging interview includes talk of this week's PHP vulnerabilities, sandboxing models in training, and OpenAI's research in mathematics.
Freedman is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware focusing on laptops, desktops and gaming.
A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others.

sources.title: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
passages: Asked about supply chain shortages, like the ongoing RAM shortage, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview that it’s “terrible” to have RAM in personal PCs instead of data centers.

Right now, memory companies Samsung and SK Hynix have long term deals with cloud service operators and projects like OpenAI’s Stargate that have reserved much of the world’s RAM output over the next few years.

sources.title: “Quite terrible”: Sam Altman says PCs waste the world’s limited DRAM supply - Notebookcheck
passages: From a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time.
You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment, - Sam Altman .
Remarks come as AI infrastructure providers compete for increasingly limited memory supplies.
Memory manufacturers are prioritizing demand from data centers, putting additional pressure on the consumer market and contributing to higher prices for PCs and other hardware.
In other words, Altman believes memory would be put to better use in centralized data centers, where it could continuously serve multiple users and workloads.
However, his argument focuses on local AI inference and does not account for the many other reasons people need RAM in their PCs, including gaming, everyday applications and multitasking.

sources.title: Sam Altman Wants Your Laptop’s RAM: Why the OpenAI CEO Says Personal Computers Are Hoarding a Scarce Resource. - Gadget Review
passages: Altman’s claim that idle consumer RAM wastes a global resource draws scrutiny given OpenAI’s direct financial stake in cloud computing
Altman reportedly argued on the Cheeky Pint podcast that local AI inference creates a poor allocation of scarce DRAM .
